title: The Silent Spire Anew
premise: Elodie Voss, a bone-carver who hears the voices of the dead in her carvings, takes in a mute child who speaks only in a language older than any kingdom — and the dead begin answering back through her. Hunted by the Crown's Wardens, who want the child destroyed to keep an ancient truce intact, Elodie and smuggler Renn Carrow flee across Thornfell toward the Silent Spire, where the child's people were entombed alive centuries ago. Elodie must choose between returning the child to the law that will kill them and waking the entombed dead, which could reignite a war. In the end she defies both Crown and Spire: she frees the sleepers' voices without waking their bodies, forging a fragile new covenant — and finds belonging not in blood or duty, but in the family she built on the road.
about_author: Ivo Almeida is the pen name of a former stonemason from the northern valleys who turned to fantasy after a decade of carving epitaphs for strangers. Their work is known for quiet protagonists, haunted landscapes, and the stubborn belief that mercy outlasts empires.

chapters.title: The Knucklebone Winter
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. In her mountain workshop, Elodie carves a dead woman's finger-bone and hears her last words — a routine grief-service for coin. Establishes her gift, her isolation, and her careful neutrality among smugglers and Wardens alike. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: A Knock at Dusk
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A half-frozen child appears at her door during a blizzard, speaking no known tongue yet humming melodies that make Elodie's finished carvings whisper. She takes the child in against every instinct for survival. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness cracking open a closed life.

chapters.title: What the Bones Remember
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The child, whom she names Ash, touches a carved jawbone and the dead speak a language predating kingdoms — one Elodie's gift translates in fragments. The bones warn of 'the Spire waking.' Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Warden's Courtesy
chapters.summary: Warden-Sergeant Corvane's POV. A polite, terrifying inspection of the valley follows rumors of 'old-tongue singing.' Corvane burns a smuggler's cache and questions Elodie, who lies well. Emotional beat: the cold machinery of duty revealed.

chapters.title: Renn's Road
chapters.summary: Renn Carrow's POV. The smuggler arrives to collect a debt and finds Elodie packing. He agrees to move them through Thornfell for reasons he won't admit — he owes Ash's people something. Emotional beat: guilt wearing charm as armor.

chapters.title: Leaving the Valley
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. They slip out ahead of the Wardens; Elodie burns her workshop to erase evidence of Ash. Grief for the only home she's known. Emotional beat: sacrifice as severance.

chapters.title: The Toll of Names
chapters.summary: Ash's POV (rendered in sensation and image). Ash remembers fragments: towers, fire, being chosen to carry the language out. First full hint that Ash escaped a living tomb. Emotional beat: homesickness for a place that was a prison.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Justice
chapters.summary: Renn's POV. At a waystation, bandits prey on refugees; Renn enforces his own brutal code when the law is absent. Elodie sees both his darkness and his decency. Emotional beat: justice outside the law has teeth and costs.

chapters.title: Voices in the Pass
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. High in Thornfell, the mountain itself hums with the old language — the dead here are older and angrier. Ash quiets them by singing. Emotional beat: awe at a heritage larger than kingdoms.

chapters.title: Corvane Closes In
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Interrogating a captured smuggler, he learns of the burned workshop and issues kill-orders framed as mercy. His own buried doubt surfaces briefly. Emotional beat: duty devouring conscience.

chapters.title: The Bone-Reader's Bargain
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A village bone-reader recognizes Elodie's gift and offers passage in exchange for hearing her murdered son's last words. Elodie pays the price and hates herself for hesitating. Emotional beat: the ethics of a gift that cannot refuse.

chapters.title: Ash Speaks
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Under stress, Ash finally speaks words Elodie understands: 'They are not dead. They are waiting. I was sent to decide.' The secret's true weight lands. Emotional beat: terror of responsibility inherited too young.

chapters.title: The Truce of Ash and Iron
chapters.summary: Renn's POV. Around a fire, Renn tells the history: six hundred years ago the Spire-folk were sealed alive beneath their tower to end a war, and the Crown's first act was enforcing that seal. Emotional beat: the past as an open wound everyone agreed to stop looking at.

chapters.title: Ambush at Greyford Bridge
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. Wardens ambush them at the bridge; Renn holds the span while Elodie and Ash escape downstream. A young Warden dies seeing Ash's face and faltering. Emotional beat: violence that leaves everyone diminished.

chapters.title: River of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Drifting downstream, wounded, they're sheltered by river-folk who owe nothing and give anyway. Elodie begins understanding belonging as something made, not granted. Emotional beat: grace from strangers.

chapters.title: Corvane's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. His superiors reveal the Wardens have always known the Spire-folk live — the seal is maintenance, not memory. Corvane's faith cracks. Emotional beat: the moment obedience becomes complicity.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Lie
chapters.summary: Renn's POV. A mapmaker who once sold Renn out offers the true route to the Spire — through the Weeping Galleries — but demands Ash as payment. Renn refuses and makes an enemy. Emotional beat: loyalty priced against survival.

chapters.title: Fever and Forgiveness
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Ash sickens; delirious, Ash calls Elodie by a name from the old tongue meaning 'mother-of-voices.' Elodie, who never wanted children, weeps. Emotional beat: love arriving uninvited and undeniable.

chapters.title: Into the Weeping Galleries
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. They enter flooded caverns where the walls are carved with millions of names — a necropolis of the silenced. The dead here do not whisper; they plead. Emotional beat: claustrophobic horror shot through with pity.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Road
chapters.summary: Renn's POV. The mapmaker sells their route to Corvane. Renn discovers it too late and must choose between warning the others and securing their exit. Emotional beat: guilt compounding like debt.

chapters.title: What Duty Owes
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Closing in, Corvane reads the original seal-decree and finds a clause no one obeys: the Spire-folk may be freed if 'a voice of theirs returns willing.' His orders say destroy the voice. Emotional beat: a man realizing his whole career is a crime.

chapters.title: The Dead Vote
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Deep in the galleries, the entombed dead reach Elodie all at once — thousands of voices arguing over whether to wake or forgive. Ash must translate a verdict. Emotional beat: democracy among ghosts.

chapters.title: Splitting the Party
chapters.summary: Renn's POV. Wardens breach the galleries; Renn draws them off alone, buying time, knowing it may cost him. Farewell without goodbye. Emotional beat: sacrifice offered quietly.

chapters.title: The Long Dark
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie and Ash descend to the Spire's sealed heart while pursuit echoes above. Ash confesses fear of what waking might unleash — including what the sleepers might do to Ash for leaving. Emotional beat: courage as walking forward while shaking.

chapters.title: Renn's Last Road
chapters.summary: Renn's POV. Captured, Renn stalls Corvane with the truth about the decree clause, turning several Wardens. Beaten but unbowed. Emotional beat: a rogue discovering conviction.

chapters.title: The Sealed Heart
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Before the great door, carved from a single vertebra of the mountain, Elodie hears the first sleeper: still alive after six centuries, sustained by the seal, begging not for freedom but for choice. Emotional beat: horror transfigured into compassion.

chapters.title: Corvane's Choice
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Arriving with Renn as prisoner, Corvane stands before the door with orders to kill Ash. He lowers his blade and arrests his own superior instead. Emotional beat: duty fulfilled rightly at last.

chapters.title: The Turning of the Key
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. Ash sings the opening verse; the seal responds not to bloodline but to willingness. The door opens onto sleeping faces, breathing dust. Emotional beat: a child shouldering an empire's sin and setting it down.

chapters.title: Voices Rising
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The sleepers wake — and the dead of the galleries rise with them in voice if not flesh. War seems certain until the eldest sleeper hears Ash's account and asks the question no one asked six hundred years ago: 'What do you want now?' Emotional beat: the cliff-edge between vengeance and covenant.

chapters.title: The Parliament of Dust
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. Sleepers, Wardens, smugglers, and villagers negotiate in the Spire hall. Old hatreds flare; Elodie's translations carry more than words — they carry intent, forcing honesty. Emotional beat: politics as translation.

chapters.title: Terms of the Anew
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The covenant is struck: the Spire-folk return as voices and stewards, not conquerors; the Crown renounces the seal; Ash becomes the first Speaker-ambassador. Elodie refuses any title. Emotional beat: peace as hard-won, imperfect craft.

chapters.title: The Price Paid
chapters.summary: Renn's POV. Wounds taken in the galleries turn serious. Renn survives, barely, and learns Elodie stayed at his side through the worst nights. Emotional beat: love admitted at last, plainly.

chapters.title: Reckonings Above Ground
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Corvane testifies against the Warden hierarchy; some days justice looks like ruin. He requests reassignment to guarding the road, not the secret. Emotional beat: a man rebuilding himself from honest rubble.

chapters.title: Homecoming, Unwanted
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Returning to her valley, Elodie finds her burned workshop already rebuilt by neighbors — the same ones who never quite welcomed her. Belonging arrives sideways. Emotional beat: tears at ordinary kindness.

chapters.title: The Child Who Decided
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. Offered a hero's place in the Spire, Ash chooses instead to stay with Elodie part of each year, keeping both worlds. Emotional beat: agency reclaimed from destiny.

chapters.title: Carving the New Names
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie carves the gallery names into standing stones across Thornfell so the dead are heard in daylight now. Her gift changes: the dead no longer haunt her; they consult her. Emotional beat: vocation transformed from burden to bridge.

chapters.title: Letters from the Spire
chapters.summary: Renn's POV. Epistolary interlude: correspondence between the trio over a year — trade routes reopening, old-tongue songs in taverns, Corvane's grudging letters. Emotional beat: warmth of a found family at distance.

chapters.title: The Quiet Anniversary
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. One year on, the three return to the Spire for the remembrance. Ash leads the singing; the mountain answers gently now. Emotional beat: grief integrated, joy earned.

chapters.title: What the Living Owe
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A new knock at the door: another child, another impossible thing. Elodie opens it without hesitation this time. Emotional beat: the arc completed — from closed door to open one.

chapters.title: The Silent Spire, Sounding
chapters.summary: Ensemble finale. The Spire rings for the first time in six centuries, its silence ended not by war but by witness. Elodie, Renn, and Ash stand together on the ridge, three kinds of outsider become one kind of home. Emotional beat: belonging as a thing built, kept, and shared.
